$comment: Emergency outreach (T-0947): the owner's assistant texts and calls the owner's own emergency contacts.
The plugin (hermes/plugins/jarvis-emergency) holds the list and the policy; the phone holds the countdown,
the location and the send. One device command, `emergency_alert`, carries the contacts and what happened.
The phone shows a countdown (and the text that will be sent) that a tap cancels, then texts every contact
the `message` with its own last fix as a map link (or `where_unknown`) and the time, and calls the first
contact. `{owner}` is filled by the phone with the words "the owner": the phone does not know a name and
the plugin does not send one. It never texts or calls a number in `never_numbers`: this does not stand in
for the emergency number, which the phone's own SOS reaches. The phone refuses a second alert within
`latch_s` seconds of one it sent, a `countdown_s` outside countdown_s..countdown_max_s is clamped, a number
with fewer than `min_digits` digits is refused, and a `what` holding a link, an address, a domain or
`min_digits` digits with no letter between them is refused: every `what_refused` by both sides, every
`what_allowed` by neither (the plugin filters too; the phone does not rely on it). Read by
message: Emergency alert from {owner}'s assistant: {what} Location: {where}. Sent {time}. This is an automated message; please call them.
what_allowed: Fell on the 3rd floor, room 204, at 12:30.
The smoke alarm is sounding. Nobody answers.
